screens.name: Home — available omen, normal and enlarged
screens.evidence: Sheets 18–27 show matching Chromium/WebKit layouts, and supplied runtime evidence verifies contrast, scrolling and navigation clearance.
findings: Increase the normal-size omen’s prominence slightly so the useful daily content feels less subordinate to the orb.

screens.name: Home — unavailable omen and expanded policy
screens.evidence: Sheets 20–27 and 48 show unavailable and expanded-policy states with a separate remaining-reading balance.
findings: Explain the separate omen allowance directly beside the failure message so “Free attempt used” and “1 left” do not require reconciliation through a disclosure.

screens.name: Home — omen loading, storage error and recovery
screens.evidence: Sheets 69 and 80 show distinct loading/storage messages, while supplied runtime evidence describes durable-claim protection and 60-second recovery.
findings: Keep the storage-retry message as visually prominent as the ordinary unavailable-omen message.

screens.name: Question entry — type or speak
screens.evidence: Sheets 28, 30–31 and 80 show a clear typing action, speech alternative and corresponding transition captures.
findings: Retain the compact orb treatment at enlarged text because both entry choices remain easy to find.

screens.name: Voice entry — could not start
screens.evidence: Sheets 49 and 81 show an explicit microphone failure with typing and retry alternatives; actual speech behavior is mocked.
findings: Give the failure explanation more prominence than the decorative introductory heading.

screens.name: Question composer — myself and named person
screens.evidence: Sheets 12, 31–33, 79 and 81 show retained questions and person summaries, with supplied browser evidence for draft and focus preservation.
findings: Replace the broad “saved details” disclosure with a concise route to the actual context that will be sent.

screens.name: Named-person selector
screens.evidence: Sheet 32 shows Someone selected, an associated first-name field, explicit confirmation and a privacy explanation at both text sizes.
findings: Preserve the explicit confirmation step and visible assurance that the named person is not notified.

screens.name: Question composer — constrained viewport and long input
screens.evidence: Sheets 15 and 29–30 show internally scrolling inputs with reachable actions, supported by the supplied 24-combination browser checks.
findings: Keep the expansion action adjacent to the input so long questions remain easy to review before submission.

screens.name: Expanded question and custom-answer editors
screens.evidence: Sheets 16–17 show Cancel, Done and scroll cues at two viewport heights, with supplied evidence for full drafts and repeated focus regression checks.
findings: Add a little internal scroll padding so partially visible lines do not sit tightly against the rounded input border.

screens.name: AI consent — review entry, disclosure and decision
screens.evidence: Sheets 14–15 show permission categories and separate Allow/Not now actions, while the supplied named-provider preview verifies request separation and retained drafts.
findings: Bring the purpose and provider into one concise introductory sentence before the category list.

screens.name: Follow-up choices — initial cards 1, 2 and 3
screens.evidence: Sheets 33–35, 78 and 84 show unselected radio options, step counts and disabled continuation, with supplied keyboard and target-size verification.
findings: Reduce the visible mist texture behind option rows to match the calmer selected-feedback screens.

screens.name: Follow-up choices — selected, keyboard focus and final Reveal
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–5 and 36–37 show distinct focus and selection states, and supplied runtime evidence verifies one commit/request plus restored selection.
findings: Preserve the separate selection and Continue/Reveal actions and the non-color selected indicator.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty, populated and constrained
screens.evidence: Sheets 29 and 35–36 show empty guidance, populated answers, expansion and reachable continuation at enlarged text.
findings: Clarify the difference between the top back arrow and “Back to choices,” which currently compete as adjacent exits.

screens.name: Reading generation — planning, research and long wait
screens.evidence: Sheets 56–57, 81 and 84 distinguish generation stages and extended waiting, with supplied cancellation and timeout evidence.
findings: Keep the stage description and safe-cancellation reassurance more prominent than the atmospheric background.

screens.name: Reading failure — planning, prediction and timeout
screens.evidence: Sheets 41–43, 82 and 85 show retry/edit/review paths, although the real-drive connection error omits the explicit no-charge reassurance shown elsewhere.
findings: Include the no-reading-spent reassurance consistently in the real connection-error state.

screens.name: Sensitive-question redirect
screens.evidence: Sheets 60–61, 79 and 82 show support or alternative-question paths and explicit no-spend/no-memory feedback.
findings: Place the humane explanation before the external-support action so the recommended next step has immediate context.

screens.name: Forecast opening — ordinary, golden, skipped and reduced motion
screens.evidence: Sheets 70–75 show opening and settled states, supported by seven verified browser paths and a retained isolated Share frame stall.
findings: Repeat the opening-to-Share performance check to determine whether the retained 200ms stall can recur.

screens.name: Forecast — settled and expanded actions
screens.evidence: Sheets 57–60 and 70–75 show the forecast, speculative label, reminder and secondary actions in normal and enlarged layouts.

screens.name: Free forecast explanation — context, assumption and limits
screens.evidence: Sheets 5–6, 79 and 81 show explicit context/assumption/limits sections and a separate Plus boundary, supported by actual Ollama-reader checks.

screens.name: Plus reading-details index

screens.name: Reading-details reader — answers

screens.name: Reading-details reader — assumptions

screens.name: Reading-details reader — saved legacy explanation

screens.name: Check-in — initial, unsaved, saved and corrected outcomes

screens.name: Check-in — expanded original question

screens.name: Sky — theme discovery and selected sample question

screens.name: History — empty

screens.name: History — populated

limitations: All scores are provisional browser assessments based on the supplied screenshots and runtime account; no independent live interaction or trace inspection was performed.
Equivalent widths, text sizes and transitions are grouped with their corresponding settled screen; numerical scores apply to the represented state family.
A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility; overall is 0.4A + 0.6F, excluding genuinely inapplicable dimensions.
The authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold is not met across every screen and component; multiple observed hierarchy, density and clarity issues remain.
No hard-gate failure is established by the supplied evidence; off-screen content in scrolled or enlarged captures is not treated as unreachable where browser reachability is explicitly verified.
Static transition captures show coherent visual roles but cannot independently prove timing, interruption behavior or smoothness.
The retained isolated 200ms Share frame gap remains unresolved despite a clean subsequent run, limiting confidence in repeatable browser performance.

Physical iPhone, Dynamic Type, native keyboard, VoiceOver, native frame rate, OS sharing/clipboard, notifications and real payments remain deferred boundaries without deductions solely for their absence.
Authenticated Circles behavior is unverified because Supabase is unconfigured; the Circle scores assess only the demonstrated offline surface and recovery.
Synthetic long-content fixtures establish layout coverage, not production-copy quality, model quality or predictive accuracy.
Repeated novice-use outcomes are not supplied, so exemplary task performance is not demonstrated.
topFixes: Clarify the separate omen allowance beside failure feedback and preserve a visible reading-specific balance label.
Reduce oversized secondary headings and excessive spacing in enlarged Circles, birth-chart, plans and check-in layouts.
Make recovery primary: demote Done on export failure and demote Copy when copying is unavailable.
Standardize navigation versus disclosure chevrons and simplify duplicated sharing-text routes.
Use calmer mist behind text-heavy tasks and meaningful labels/boundaries in stored evidence readers.
Repeat the isolated opening-to-Share performance scenario and retain any recurrence of the 200ms stall.
